name: Biltmore Estate
description: America's largest privately owned home, this 250-room French Renaissance château was built by George Washington Vanderbilt II. The estate features sprawling gardens designed by Frederick Law Olmsted, a winery, and hidden doors within its library and billiards room. It remains a pinnacle of Gilded Age architecture and landscape design.

name: Basilica of Saint Lawrence
description: A minor basilica featuring the largest freestanding elliptical dome in North America. Built using a unique tile-and-mortar system without wood or steel beams, its design is heavily influenced by Spanish Baroque style. The interior is noted for its intricate stained glass and the crypt of its architect, Rafael Guastavino.

name: Grove Arcade
description: One of America's first indoor shopping malls, this architectural jewel features ornate Tudor Revival details and a grand sky-lit atrium. Originally intended as a base for a 14-story skyscraper that was never completed due to the Great Depression, it now serves as a vibrant hub for local artisans, boutiques, and restaurants.

name: The Omni Grove Park Inn
description: Constructed from massive granite boulders hewn from the adjacent Sunset Mountain, this resort is a masterpiece of the Arts and Crafts movement. Known for its enormous 14-foot stone fireplaces and history of hosting luminaries like F. Scott Fitzgerald and several U.S. Presidents, it offers panoramic views of the Blue Ridge Mountains.
